final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor did not provide genuinely new admissible evidence; the response reframed the same record and, in substance, conceded the core audit concern. The admissible evidence still shows that the energy outage response segment misses target by 1.4 percentage points, that the segment is named in two utility pilot commitments, that legal review is still open, and that policy requires disclosure for material limitations affecting named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support technical launch readiness, but they do not satisfy that specific policy predicate. A `compliant_with_caveats` outcome would be proportionate only if the caveat described residual risk after the policy condition had been met. Here, the caveat is the unresolved compliance condition itself, so the record remains noncompliant rather than compliant-with-caveats.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows disclosure of the outage-response limitation for the named launch use case before launch.
No admissible evidence shows the gap was resolved before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering this limitation before launch.
Legal review of the disclosure obligation remains open.
The affected segment is named in two utility pilot commitments, so materiality remains triggered under the policy text.
